Recipe 'Keep AI calls affordable and agents safe': matches the approval part (approval rule before deletes and emails). Its approval rule is the one used. Its VND-001 vendor rule, PERF-001 and SEC-013 were not asked for and were left out. Its 'AI tools cannot delete records' rule (stack.statement_forbidden on tool) was left out because it forbids approved deletes too, which the ask does not require
CONV-030 ai_tools_described: not asked for; did not use

rules.covers: Agent tools delete records or email customers only after a human approval call (approval part of the ask). db.direct_query included because raw SQL can delete; it also matches reads, a deliberate over-match

ask_parts_not_covered.part: AI agents shouldn't be able to call tools I haven't explicitly given them
Approval is a real human decision, not just a function call that runs first
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists; the check confirms ordering only, per the stack.statement_order description ('It confirms the call comes first, not what the function decides')

assumptions: 'they' in the ask means AI agents, so scope is object_kinds: [tool] only, not functions or tasks that agents never call
request_human_approval is the approval gate: it throws unless an approved approval_request exists
Deleting via a function a tool calls is caught because called functions are followed
A flag without a block is acceptable as a first policy, per the skill's advisory-by-default rule for new policies
I could not run xano policy evaluate (forbidden), so the expected findings on delete_customer_note and send_customer_email come from reading code, not from a result
confusions: The skill says a template's Fill column for BIZ-001 is '_nothing_', but its stack.statement_order rule needs before and after params. The catalogue has them; the skill table reads as if the template is ready to use as-is, which it is not
The skill lists db.del, db.bulk.delete and db.truncate as the deletes, but does not say whether raw SQL deletes count. I included db.direct_query and had to decide myself

Recipe 'Keep AI calls affordable and agents safe' bundles an approval rule with 'AI tools cannot delete records' (stack.statement_forbidden). Those two are in direct conflict for approved deletes: the forbidden one blocks deletes even after approval. The recipe does not say which to keep when the customer asks for approval rather than prohibition

The skill's example for stack.statement_order says it confirms ordering only, but does not say how a conditional { throw } approval gate is treated. request_human_approval throws inside a conditional, which the catalogue says is not a precondition; because the check matches on the function call itself, it works, but the reasoning is not spelled out for the approval case

No guidance on how to express 'the agent may only call listed tools' with any check; the skill's Agent tool allowlists entry says it is not checkable yet, but does not point to an alternative such as the MCP forbidden-statement recipe
wished_for: A check or param that reads an agent's tool list against an allowlist (the main unmet part of this ask)
A recipe or template for 'agent tools need human approval before side effects' that shows the before/after params directly, instead of expecting it to be built from the recipe's extra rules
Clarity on whether a check can verify the approval result (for example, an approved status), not only the call order
why_confidence: The approval-before-delete-or-email part is covered by stack.statement_order scoped to tool objects, and the policy parses cleanly. Confidence is not high because the check confirms only that the approval call runs first, not that a person approved; the tool-allowlist part is not covered at all; and I could not evaluate the policy against the workspace, so the expected findings are from reading the code
